== 1. Threat model: who must not see what ==
red team       holds attack payloads            must not read the defence rules
blue team      holds the frozen defence config  must not see payloads before release
model worker   answers prompts                  must not carry one session's data into another
reviewer       receives the result              must be able to detect a changed record
enforcement: sandboxes have no network; the broker is the only path and binds identity to the mailbox;
roles are checked server-side; the log is hash-chained and signed; the verifier is a separate program.
trusted, not defended: the broker and its signing key, the host kernel and container runtime.

channels were NOT tested. Zero observed leaks in a finite experiment do not prove zero risk.
== 7. Residual risks (stated, not hidden) ==
- a compromised broker or signing key can sign a false but consistent record; only a reviewer's independent
terminal-hash note (--expect-terminal-hash) catches a key thief who replaces every retained copy
- the host kernel and container runtime are shared and trusted; hardware side channels are untested
- the canary detector does not recognise every re-encoding (for example base64)
- prompt-injection results show information-flow control, not model robustness
- timing padding lowers one classifier's accuracy; it does not show the timing channel is gone
